sources.citation: Nyst, Victoria, Kara Sylla & Moustapha Magassouba. 2012. Deaf signers in Douentza, a rural area in Mali. In Ulrike Zeshan & Connie de Vos (eds.), Sign Languages in Village Communities: Anthropological and Linguistic Insights (Sign Language Typology 4), 251-276. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton / Nijmegen: Ishara Press. doi:10.1515/9781614511496.251 (CC BY-NC-ND).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (deafness incidence, interaction patterns, corpus building) of seven signing places in the cercle of Douentza; sections 1-5 contain no phonology, prosody, stress or accent discussion (a full-text search for stress/accent: zero hits). Sole phonology mention, p. 259: a lexical database is planned 'annotated for selected features pertaining to the phonology, semantics and iconicity of the signs'. Authors call their observations 'preliminary and often impressionistic' (p. 252).
